The appellant has filed this appeal U/Sec.29 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the respondent challenging the order dated 28-09- 2016 passed in Cr.Misc.51/2011 on the file of Court of M.M.T.C-IV, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: Appellant is the R.1 and respondent is the petitioner before the trial court.
Therefore, for the sake of convenience, the parties to this 2 Crl.A.1559/2016 appeal are herein afterwards referred with their ranks before the trial Court.

2. The brief facts as set out in the memorandum of appeal are that before the trial Court, the petitioner has filed petition under Secs.12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act,
2005 against the R.1 to 4 seeking reliefs under Secs.19, 20 and 22 of the Act contending that she is the legally wedded wife of R.1 in view of solemnization of her marriage with him on 08-11-2000 at Dwarakanath Bhawan.

Therefore, after her marriage, R.1 has started to harass her for dowry.

sentences.text: He deprived her of food, cloth and affection by inflicting physical and mental cruelty on her.
Therefore, she has filed a complaint against R.1 to 4 before the Subramanyanagara Police Station.
Police have enquired the residents and has warned them not to cause domestic violence on her.
But, the respondents have continued their acts of causing domestic violence on her.
She has contended that the respondents owned a house.
The 1 st respondent is having a wholesale business of medicine.
He has sufficient source of income.
In spite of it, the respondents have neglected and refused to provide basic needs to her and her child.
Therefore, she is in need of Rs.50,000/- p.m as maintenance.
She has sought for grant 3 Crl.A.1559/2016 of Rs.2 lakhs as compensation towards the domestic violence caused by the respondents on her.
Therefore, she has sought for grant of the reliefs as prayed against R.1 to 4 before the trial Court.

3. On service of notice of the said petition, R.1 to 4 have put their appearance before the trial Court through their Advocate and have filed their common written objections contending that the petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.12(1) of PWDV Act is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
They have admitted that marriage of the petitioner was solemnized with R.1 on 08-11-2000 at Dwaraka Bhavan, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru.
R.1 is residing in a rented house along with his parents and brothers and running a small medical store. R.1 to 4 have denied all other specific allegations that made against them as false.

They have contended that R.1 has received one gold ring weighing 5 grams, one bracelet weighing 12 grams, chain weighing 8 grams, one colour TV, one fridge, TV Stand only from the parents of the petitioner.
He has not received any cash nor demanded the petitioner to give cash and other gold items as alleged.
The R.1 to 4 have specifically denied that they demanded the petitioner to pay dowry amount, gold and silver articles as alleged.
They also have specifically denied that they subjected the petitioner to a domestic violence as alleged in the petition.

The respondents have contended that after the marriage, the petitioner had stayed with R.1 only up to February-2001 4 Crl.A.1559/2016 thereafter she had left the company of R.1 and has gone to her parents house voluntarily for the reason best known to her.
Thereafter, R.1 has made a separate house and that she returned on 01-11-2012 and stayed with him up to 23- 11-2011 and went back to her parents house.
During that time, she lived with him happily.
The R.1 had only Bank balance of Rs.3,705/- as on 26-07-2000.
The petitioner is getting a monthly rental income of more than Rs.40 to 50 thousand.
The 1st respondent's mother is undergoing medical treatment.
R.1 himself spending money towards her medical treatment.
At the time of marriage, R.1 gave 100 grams of gold jewelry including other silver items and 5 costly silk sarees with 20 grams of Mangalasuthra to the petitioner.
The respondents have pleaded that the petitioner has filed the petition just to harass them.
A dispute is pending before the Family Court at Bengaluru.
The petitioner has collected a sum of Rs.4 lakhs as on the date of complaint saying that she will deposit it in the name of her daughter.
But, she has not mentioned anything about receipt of the said money.

The respondents have further pleaded that just to take advantage of the fact, though MC petition is pending before the Family Court, the petitioner has filed this petition though she is having sufficient income.
The respondents are having very meager income.
Therefore, the respondents are all have sought for dismissal of the petition filed by the petitioner.

sentences.text: Before the trial Court, the petitioner herself got examined as PW.1 and examined one Ramugopal as PW.2.
She got exhibited 20 documents as Ex's.P.1 to 20 and closed her side of evidence to substantiate her claim.

R.1 only examined as RW.1 and has got exhibited 5 documents as Ex's.R.1 to 5 and closed his side of evidence to substantiate defence of R.1 to 4.
5.

On considering the petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.12 of PWDV Act, the objections of R.1 to 4, evidence of PW's.1 and 2, RW.1, contents of Ex's.P.1 to 20 and Ex's.R.1 to 5 and upon considering the arguments urged before it, the trial Court has partly allowed the petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.12 of the DV Act.

The trial Court has directed the 1st respondent to pay Rs.6,000/- p.m to the petitioner and Rs.4,000/- p.m to her daughter as maintenance from the date of petition till his marriage subsists with the petitioner and that his daughter gets married.
The trial Court also has directed the R.1 to pay Rs.3 lakhs to the petitioner as compensation.
The trial Court has dismissed the petition of the petitioner that filed in respect of passing of residence order etc.

The trial Court also had dismissed the petition as against R.2 to 4.
6.
Being aggrieved by the impugned order of the trial Court, R.1 has filed this appeal contending that the impugned order of the trial Court is bad in law and the materials placed on record.
The trial Court has committed grave error in not properly considering the objections, 6 Crl.A.1559/2016 evidence and arguments of R.1.

The trial Court has committed grave error in coming to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.8,000/- p.m as interim maintenance though she is capable of earning and having sufficient source of income.
The trial Court has not considered the evidence and without going through the documents furnished by him, has passed the impugned order.

The trial Court has not considered the fact that R.1 is only getting income of Rs.2,000/-
approximately and except that, he has no other source of income.
The trial Court has ignored that R.1 has to incur the medical expenses of his aged mother who is suffering from cancer disease.
Therefore, payment of Rs.8,000/- p.m as interim maintenance is beyond his control.
The trial Court has ignored that the application filed by the petitioner under Sec.12 of PWDV Act is not maintainable.
The trial Court has ignored that the petitioner has not produced any document to prove the income of R.1.
The trial Court has passed the impugned order without application of its judicious mind.
The trial Court has ignored that the petitioner has filed the said application just to harass him and to make him to heed her illegal demands.
The petitioner has not produced any documents showing his monthly income but the trial Court has not considered it.
The petitioner has not produced any documents showing her own income.
The trial Court has not appreciated the facts that admitted during the course of cross-examination of petitioner.
The impugned order is 7 Crl.A.1559/2016 based on inference and presumption, which is liable to be set-aside.
Hence, this appeal.

Along with the appeal, the R.1 has filed IA under Sec.5 of Limitation Act for condonation of delay of 62 days in filing this appeal contending that his mother is suffering from bone cancer and that therefore he is unable to contact his Advocate.
7. After service of notice of this appeal, the petitioner has put her appearance through her counsel.
Record of the trial Court is secured.
The petitioner has not filed any objections to the IA filed under Sec.5 of Limitation Act.
After filing of this appeal, R.1 and his counsel are remained as absent.

As per the final order for the following REASONS 11. POINT NO.1:- It is the case of R.1 that he has sufficient cause to condone delay of 62 days in filing this appeal.
In the affidavit, R.1 has contended that his Advocate has applied for grant of certified copy of order on 07-10- 2016.
Office has prepared the copies on 19-11-2016.
His 9 Crl.A.1559/2016 mother is suffering from back bone cancer.
Therefore, he is unable to contact his Advocate till 19-12-2016.
Therefore, there was such delay in filing this appeal.
The petitioner has not filed objections nor opposed this application seriously.
The grounds urged appears to be genuine grounds.
Hence, delay can be condoned.
No hardship would be caused to the petitioner because she has right to contest the appeal on merits.
If delay is not condoned, the R.1 would be put to irreparable loss and injury which cannot be compensated in terms of damages.
Therefore, this court has answered point No.1 in the affirmative.
12. POINTS NO.2 to 5:
These points are inter- linked with each other therefore these points are taken together for joint discussion to avoid repetition of facts.
Before going to discuss these points, it is necessary to refer relevant Sections of PWDV Act.

4 As per Sec.2(a) of PWDV Act, 2005 aggrieved person means any women who is, or has been in domestic relationship with the respondent and who alleges to have been subjected to any act of domestic vigilance by the respondent.

As per Sec.2(f) of PWDV Act, 2005 Domestic relationship means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of the 1 Crl.A.1559/2016 marriage,
adoption or are family member living together as joint family.
As per Sec.2(e) of PWDV Act, 2005 Domestic incident report means a report made in the prescribed form on receipt of a complaint of domestic violence from an aggrieved person.
As per Sec.2(s) of PWDV Act, 2005 shared household means a household where the person aggrieved lives or any stage has lived in a domestic relationship either singly or along with the respondent and includes such a household whether owned or tenanted either jointly by the aggrieved person and the respondent, or owned or tenanted by either of them in respect of which either the aggrieved person or the respondent or both jointly or singly have any right, title, interest and equity and includes such a household hold which may belong to the joint family of which the respondent is a member, irrespective of whether the respondent or the aggrieved person has any right, title or interest in the share household.
Sec.3 of PWDV Act, 2005 defines the meaning of Domestic Violence, which provides as under;
3. Definition of domestic violence.--For the purposes of this Act, any act, omission or commission or conduct of the respondent shall constitute domestic violence in case it-- (a) harms or injures or endangers the health, safety, life, limb or well-being, whether mental or physical, of the aggrieved person or tends to do so and includes causing physical abuse, 11 Crl.A.1559/2016 sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse and economic abuse; or (b) harasses, harms, injures or endangers the aggrieved person with a view to coerce her or any other person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any dowry or other property or valuable security; or (c) has the effect of threatening the aggrieved person or any person related to her by any conduct mentioned in clause (a) or clause (b); or (d) otherwise injures or causes harm, whether physical or mental, to the aggrieved person.
Explanation I.--For the purposes of this section,

16 . As rightly observed by the trial Court, in the cross- examination at Page No.91, PW.1 has deposed that she has filed this petition as usual.
Nothing is elicited in the cross- examination of RW.1 in support of the case of petitioner.
MC Petition was dismissed.
Hence, question of continuing maintenance in MC petition does not arise.

As petitioner has not challenged the finding of the trial Court that she has 1 Crl.A.1559/2016 failed to prove domestic violence, question of considering whether the trial Court has erred in doing so is not required.

Sec.23(2) of the Act provides that if the Magistrate is satisfied that an application prima facie disclosed that the respondent is committing an act of Domestic Violence, he may grant an order on the basis of affidavit etc.
Sec.23(1) provides that Magistrate may pass such interim order as a deems just and proper.

Sec.22 of the Act provides that the Magistrate may pass order directing the respondent to pay compensation and damages for the injuries including mental torture and emotional distress caused by the facts of domestic violence committed by that respondent.

In view of the failure of the petitioner to prove that the RW.1 to 4 have subjected her to a domestic violence, grant of Rs.3,00,000/- as compensation and maintenance at the rate of Rs.10,000/- p.m to the petitioner is incorrect and that it is against the object of the PWDV Act.
In fact, she has claimed only Rs.2,00,000/-.
Therefore, the impugned order can be set-aside.
Therefore, this Court has answered the aforesaid points No.2 to 5 as in the affirmative.
17. POINT NO.6:
Appeal filed by the appellant for R.1 U/Sec.29 of the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is hereby allowed.
The impugned order of the Trial Court dated 28.09.2016 passed in C.Misc.51/2011 on the file of Court of M.M.T.C-IV, Bengaluru, is hereby set aside.

It is hereby further ordered that the petition filed by the petitioner U/s.12 of PWDV Act is hereby dismissed.
Send back the trial Court record forth with along with the copy of this judgment.
